play.menu: state.shop ? 'shop: ' + state.shop.title + ' (' + state.shop.side + ', cursor ' + (state.shop.cursor + 1) + ')' : state.menuPage ? 'menu: ' + state.menuPage.tab + ' page' : state.mode == 'menu' || state.mode == 'shop' || state.mode == 'paused' ? state.mode : null
play.notice: (() => { const n = [state.banner, state.notice, ...(state.toasts || []).filter((t) => t.age < 2).map((t) => t.text)].filter(Boolean); return n.length ? [...new Set(n)].join('  |  ') : null; })()
play.goal: (() => { const qs = (state.quests || []).filter((x) => x.state !== 'done'); const q = qs.find((x) => x.tracked) || qs.find((x) => x.state === 'active'); if (!q) return null; const more = qs.length - 1; const text = q.title + (q.need ? ' (' + q.have + '/' + q.need + ')' : '') + (q.status ? ': ' + q.status : '') + (more > 0 ? ' [+' + more + ' other quest' + (more > 1 ? 's' : '') + ' in the journal]' : ''); return q.pos ? { text, pos: q.pos } : text; })()
play.brief: Embervale: an open-world pixel RPG (think Skyrim in pixels). Distances are in tiles. The goal line is the tracked quest and its next step; 'goto goal' walks to where that step happens (a door, a den, a camp). Public buildings are listed by their doors (Inn, Shop, Smithy, Temple...): 'goto Inn' walks in, and inside you talk to the people there (talk Innkeeper) and leave by 'goto Exit'. Entering or leaving a building interrupts the order: give the next one. Stall keepers are talked to from the front of their counter. A job you have just accepted becomes the tracked quest: the goal line, the map marker and 'goto goal' follow it (the game says NEW QUEST: ...); every open quest with a place to go is also listed as a Quest thing named by its title: goto "<title>" walks there (a den, a camp, a door). There is no block: fights roll away from telegraphed bites (dodge, the default); wolves wind up before they bite, and a badly hurt one runs off: 'fight' it again to finish it. People can be talked to; animals (hens, dogs, goats...) cannot. Dialogue options are picked with choose N; walking away or choosing FAREWELL ends a conversation; a gift handed over while someone speaks shows in the dialogue as 'gifts' and in the game-says line as '+ <NAME>'. Reading the game: what beasts drop lies on the ground as item things (RAW HIDE, VENISON, a purse of GOLD) until you walk over them: 'pickup' (or 'pickup <name>') collects them, and each one picked up says '+ <NAME>'. A shop (talk to a smith or merchant, then the trade option) is shown as screen text: your gold and the keeper's purse, the BUY list (what he sells, '<n>) NAME - PRICE GOLD', '(TOO DEAR)' when you cannot afford it), the SELL list (your pack, '(WORN)' on what you wear) the deal line ('DEAL: <ROW> - BUY FOR n GOLD', naming the row under the cursor) and the KEYS line; '>' marks the row under the cursor. Up/down move the cursor, left/right switch BUY and SELL, enter buys or sells, escape leaves. Selling a piece you wear asks first: the deal line says 'YOU WEAR IT - PRESS ENTER AGAIN TO SELL', and a second enter sells it. The menu (tab) shows its page as screen text: the tab strip with the open page in [brackets], its rows and the page's key line; Q/E switch tabs (ITEMS: the pack, '(WORN)' marks; QUESTS: the journal; EQUIP: each slot and what it wears, W/S pick a slot, A/D choose a piece for it, enter wears or takes it off). The place stat reads '<PLACE> - LEVEL n, DANGER +d (YOU ARE LEVEL m)': the place's level, and danger is that level less yours: danger 5 or more (a ruin's or cave's level inside one) means the foes there outclass you; the place stat then ends '- DANGEROUS GROUND', and on the way in the game says 'DANGEROUS GROUND / <NAME>: LEVEL n - YOU ARE LEVEL m'. A game call that stays busy (a walk, or a setup call that is still travelling) is stopped with 'call cancel'; the session's own stop ends the whole run.
